content: The snow goose need not bathe to make itself white. Neither need you do anything but be yourself.
author: Alan Watts
sourceWork: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are (1966)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

In Alan Watts's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
